question: Verify whether the lines $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}=(4\hat{i}+2\hat{j})+\mu(\hat{i}+\hat{j})$ are coplanar. Give mathematical justification.
explanation:
Step 1: Identification of position and direction vectors
For the first line, $\vec{a}_1=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}_1=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$. For the second line, $\vec{a}_2=4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}$ and $\vec{b}_2=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$.
Step 2: Vector joining points on the two lines
$$\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1=3\hat{i}+\hat{k}.$$
Step 3: Coplanarity condition
Two lines are coplanar if
$$\left(\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1\right)\cdot\left(\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2\right)=0.$$
Step 4: Vector product and scalar product
$$\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2=(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})\times(\hat{i}+\hat{j})=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}.$$
Therefore,
$$\left(3\hat{i}+\hat{k}\right)\cdot\left(-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\right)=-3+3=0.$$
Step 5: Final conclusion
Since the required scalar triple product is zero, the given lines are coplanar.

options.A: The lines are not coplanar because the scalar triple product is $6$.
options.B: The lines are parallel and hence coplanar.
options.C: The lines are coplanar because $(\vec a_2-\vec a_1)\cdot(\vec b_1\times\vec b_2)=0$.
options.D: The lines are skew because their direction vectors are not proportional.
